description:
Signal: cargo test --test fz2_cli fails on Enum fixtures. enum_take_positive_single and enum_predicate_search fail Cranelift verification because a call supplies four arguments to a five-argument callable signature. enum_take_drop_split fails native callable materialization because one clause receives incompatible physical ABI resolutions.

Root cause: executable/transport symbols originally erased ActivationKey.arrow, so direct and closure-call materialization could select a sibling specialization with the same function/input projection. Clause helpers also copied the owner executable ABI instead of deriving their own entry-lane ABI. Both defects are repaired in this ticket's working tree.

Blocking discovery: the remaining failures are not repairable by correlating just the return lanes. BackendCallableEntry pools one BoundaryId's call surface with a concrete target, while CallableDescr identifies a materialized closure by function/captures rather than that target's complete physical ABI. A closure can therefore receive the code pointer for a sibling activation surface. The attempted target-return split removes the JIT wrapper mismatch but re-exposes the same wrong code pointer as fz_ref_load_int(ValueRef). The complete owner model is fz-k22.20: resolved callable entry owns target capture, argument, and return ABI; materialization selects that entry. This ticket now depends on it rather than retaining an unsound partial adaptation.

Goal: restore JIT and AOT execution for the existing fz2 Enum fixture contracts without suppressing diagnostics or relaxing the CLI tests.

Verification after fz-k22.20: enum_take_positive_single, enum_take_drop_split, and enum_predicate_search run/build; cargo test --test fz2_cli; cargo test --lib; strict clippy.

comments.text: fz-k22.20 deletion audit: `enum_take_drop_split` reaches a source publication position for CallableId(19) with BoundaryIds(4,5), but BoundaryId(4) still owns two concrete entries (targets 162/163) with the same physical ABI. Native now correctly refuses to invent a code pointer. The missing fact is upstream: publication must carry one exact callable-entry identity, or semantic/transport must split this pooled multi-specialization value before packaging. No native fallback or target/type re-selection remains.

title: Repair native Enum callable ABI regressions exposed by fz2 CLI
